question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}+3x & =3{x}^{3}-4x \\ {x}^{3}+3x & =-4x \\ {x}^{3}+7x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $x.$ We can factor out the $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+7x & =0 \\ x({x}^{2}+7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}^{2}+7=0$ has no real solutions, we cannot factor the expression ${x}^{2}+7$  further.

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the only solution is $x=0.$
